parsed.summary: jane welsh came to tell him that she was gone from her master and resolved to stick to her sweetheart, harbing. he tried in a word or two to dissuade her, then spent an hour or two talking with her after sending her away and meeting her again near the exchange and the three cranes. he urged her to make herself happy by staying out her time with her master and gave other counsels, but she said she could not do it, because it was her fortune to have this man, though she believed it would be to her ruine. afterward he returned to his business, dined with mr. povy and creed, visited lord bellasses and white hall, delivered a letter to the duke of yorke, talked with mr. slingsby about the mint and coynage of money, then came home, saw sir j. minnes sick, and ended the day at his office and supper.

canon.summary: he spent the morning about late instructions for signing bills and paying them, and had poynter accepted as an additional clerke. at noon he was called away to dine with mr. hill and mr. houbland, then later brought mr. andrews to desire tallys for tangier victualls, by which he cleared to himself l210. in the evening he watched lord bruncker take a watch to pieces and put it back together, which pleased him greatly, though he was vexed by a snappish answer from madam williams and burdened by being pressed to continue meetings for christmas. he then made up his journall, felt his mind eased, and noted the frosty weather and hoped it might lessen the plague next week.
